scope: CSS numeric color integration; typed CPU compilation/resolution and unchanged conversion worker. No CSSOM/style/layout/GPU/UI/JS/network/browser or Chrome performance claim.
before: Unmodified committed color parser at base_commit, same color_bench source.
after: Typed static/contextual math, conservative dependencies, inline compiler scratch, shared normalization and aggregate quotas.
method: Three sequential alternating before/after runs (reversed in middle), CPU 0, 20 rounds; ordinary parsing/resolution each 20000 iterations per case; conversion 20 independently reset samples per workload. Contextual math benchmark separately runs three times: 2000 compiles and 20000 resolves per case, with prebuilt Syntax. Throughput parsing/resolution values are each run mean; summaries median of three means. Conversion summary median of three run medians. First-call samples recorded independently. No concurrent checks started by this session during measurements. Clocks/thermals/other load uncontrolled.
memory_accounting: Value/Color size and retained unique arena/Arc/program/boxed-channel capacities per separately compiled value; excludes allocator overhead, original Syntax/source and transient compiler/resolution scratch. Cloned Values share arenas and must not be added repeatedly. RSS is entire synthetic benchmark, including generated/reset conversion buffers or the 10000-value pools and allocator retention.
caveats: Feature integration has measured parsing/storage costs: no uniform throughput improvement claim.
No SIMD or GPU added here; earlier bounded SIMD conversion is unchanged. Conversion differences include machine/compiler/code-layout effects.
Inline temporary slots avoid extra allocations for the common small contextual compilation. Larger conditional function lists can spill.
Website conformance and live style invalidation are not demonstrated.
Prebuilt syntax excludes lexical/source cost. New contextual workloads have no before throughput: old parser explicitly rejects them.
